# Esther Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 456r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus — this is the Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Ethiopia, over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces —

**1:2** that in those days, when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom in the citadel of Susa,

**1:3** in the third year of his reign, he gave a banquet for all his officials and servants. The military force of Persia and Media, the nobles and governors of the provinces, were before him,

**1:4** while he displayed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the splendor of his excellent majesty for many days — one hundred and eighty days.

**1:5** When these days were completed, the king gave a banquet lasting seven days for all the people present in the citadel of Susa, from the greatest to the least, in the court of the garden of the king's palace.

**1:6** There were hangings of white cotton and blue-violet, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rods and marble pillars. The couches were of gold and silver on a mosaic pavement of alabaster, marble, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone.

**1:7** Drinks were served in golden vessels, each vessel different from the others, and the royal wine was plentiful, according to the generosity of the king.

**1:8** The drinking was done according to the rule: no one was compelled, for the king had instructed every chief steward of his household to serve each man as he desired.

**1:9** Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace of King Ahasuerus.

**1:10** On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas — the seven eunuchs who attended King Ahasuerus —

**1:11** to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, in order to display her beauty to the peoples and the officials, for she was lovely in appearance.

**1:12** But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs. Then the king became furious, and his anger burned within him.

**1:13** So the king consulted the wise men who understood the times — for this was the king's custom toward all who were versed in law and judgment.

**1:14** Those closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan — the seven officials of Persia and Media who had personal access to the king and held the highest seats in the kingdom.

**1:15** "According to law, what is to be done with Queen Vashti, since she has not obeyed the command of King Ahasuerus conveyed by the eunuchs?"

**1:16** Then Memucan declared before the king and the officials, "Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king but also all the officials and all the peoples throughout the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

**1:17** For the queen's conduct will become known to all women, and they will look on their husbands with contempt, saying, 'King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she would not come.'

**1:18** This very day, the noble women of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen's conduct will respond to all the king's officials in the same way, and there will be no end of contempt and conflict.

**1:19** If it pleases the king, let a royal decree go out from him, and let it be inscribed in the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be revoked: that Vashti shall never again come before King Ahasuerus, and let the king give her royal position to another who is more worthy than she.

**1:20** When the decree that the king issues is proclaimed throughout all his kingdom — vast as it is — then all wives will give honor to their husbands, from the greatest to the least."

**1:21** This counsel pleased the king and the officials, and the king acted according to the word of Memucan.

**1:22** He sent letters to all the king's provinces, to every province in its own script and to every people in its own language, declaring that every man should be master in his own household and speak in the language of his own people.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **Absence of the Divine Name:** The book of Esther contains no mention of God, the LORD, or any divine title. This is unique among the books of the Hebrew Bible. LOGOS preserves this silence faithfully. Readers have long observed that divine providence is present in the narrative's structure even though it is never named.

2. **"Royal decree...inscribed in the laws" (1:19):** The irrevocable nature of Persian law becomes a key narrative mechanism throughout the book. The Hebrew uses the Persian loanword *dat* rather than the typical Hebrew *torah*, grounding the legal framework in its Persian setting.

3. **"Every man should be master in his own household" (1:22):** The Hebrew *sorer* means "to rule" or "to have dominion." The irony of this decree — attempting to legislate domestic authority — sets the comedic and subversive tone that characterizes the entire book.

*— LOGOS*
